_about: Combat Lab token DICTIONARY (words for what the MWO scale chart and the 3D kits show), 2026-11-03. 'seen' lists chassis, 'status' says whether the generator has it (built / idea). Words only: nothing is copied from art. Add terms by editing this file.

wedge.what: wide rear narrowing to the front

arrow.what: very long, pointed nose (nose half the length) with rear corner tabs

oval_disc.what: wide flat oval with a thin rim flange

arms_forward.what: arm barrels or arms projecting well forward of the body, seen as long bars at both sides

slung_wedge.what: long low wedge slung forward, nose level or rising

crouched.status: built (2026-11-03, session 16): legs 16 percent shorter, knees forward, the whole upper body pitched 20 degrees about the hips
crouched.what: whole body pitched forward over bent legs, torso low

triple_hump.what: three humps along the top (head plus two shoulder boxes)

round_dome.what: torso and head one round dome

v_chest.what: hexagonal faceted chest plate between the shoulder launchers (the chart showed a V; the Mauler model shows a hexagon)

skull_head.status: built (2026-11-03, session 16): Atlas only, by named tag
skull_head.what: faceted dome head with brow ridge, two glowing eye slits, nose bridge and a mask plate for the jaw, seated in a notch at the top front of the torso; never picked by the name hash (Daniel: unique to the Atlas)

wing_spar.what: a very wide thin bar across the shoulders, round pods at its ends

ears.what: tall box missile pods rising above the shoulders

fins_swept.what: fins or horns swept outward and up from the shoulders

vertical_posts.what: tall slab posts at both shoulders (on the Mauler: the rear wings of its big shoulder launchers)

corner_pods.what: box pods at the upper outer corners of the torso

round_arm_blocks.what: big rounded blocks where the arms start

dome_pauldron.what: a faceted dome over each shoulder with a flat rim flange under it

launcher_boxes.what: huge slanted-top missile boxes on the shoulders, a cell grid on the sloped face and a tall rear wing (bigger than ears)

tall_launchers.what: two tall upright launcher boxes at the back of the shoulders, a cell grid on the front face

shoulder_gun_pods_with_arms.what: a pod on each shoulder with two long barrels forward, in addition to ordinary arms

long_barrel_arms.what: each arm one or two very long barrels pointing straight forward

ball_fists.what: huge round ball hands hanging at the sides

claw_arms.what: arms bowed outward and down like crab claws

a_frame_arms.what: arms angled outward and down from the shoulder in an A-frame

tiny_arms.what: small arms under big shoulder boxes

shoulder_gun_pods.what: twin-barrel pods at the shoulders sticking far forward (instead of arms)

pincer_hands.what: two jaws with angled tips on a palm instead of a fist

chicken (bird).what: thigh forward-down to the knee, shin back-down to a high hock, long foot with a three-toe claw (two forward, one back), hock block, knee disc cover

pillar.what: thick straight columns with little knee bend and block feet

barrel_shin.what: shin shaped like a fat barrel (the chart suggested it for the Archer; the Archer model shows ordinary plated legs, so it is unused for now)

reverse_lower_leg.what: lower leg angled back with a big heel in side view

stacked_slab.what: two stacked chamfered slabs on the thigh, three on the shin (tapering), a clamshell knee block, wide block foot

antennas.what: one to three thin masts; Zeus two tall, Locust two, Cyclops a tent of three guy wires

jump_pylons.what: tall pylons rising behind the shoulders

tent_antenna.what: three wires from a mast to the shoulders

asymmetry.what: one arm much bigger than the other, or bulkier on one side

surface_plating.what: option surface = plated / smooth: vents across the lower torso front, bolts at the chest corners, panel lines along the top, armor bands on humanoid legs
seen: every chassis (plated by default from 60 t, else by the name hash)

cockpit_scale.what: head and cockpit glass scale with the cube root of cockpit tons over total tons (a cockpit is a fixed ~3 t): x1.36 at 20 t, 1.0 at 50 t, 0.79 at 100 t, 0.64 at 200 t. Cockpit weights by type are Claude's recall of the construction rules (not in the indexed Core): standard 3, small 2, torso-mounted 4, command console 3, industrial 3, primitive 5

team_accents.what: class tm plates (chest stripe, shoulder plates, canopy bay tops) painted in the team color by the viewer; armor tinted a little; red, blue, green, gold

limb_panel_lines.what: dark panel line down the front of thigh, shin and forearm

fists_feet_heads.what: fists with a palm, three finger plates and a thumb; feet with a heel block and two toe wedges; heads by side profile (box / wedge / visor extruded, dome a blob); shoulder caps instead of balls; jump-jet nozzles wider at the mouth with a glow

tail_fin.what: a tall swept fin at the rear of the hull plus two small ones

grille_chest.what: a recessed grille panel on the chest: a frame and seven dark slats

weapon_models._about: Each weapon family has its own 3D model, chosen from the weapon's name (weapon_fam in INTEGRATION__tokens.py). Sizes are in pixels so weapons keep a fixed scale (they look larger on small 'Mechs). The receiver is buried in the part the weapon mounts on.

laser.what: housing with a heat-fin plate and a lens in the energy color; pulse lasers get two lenses; small / medium / large by size

ppc.what: long barrel with three coil rings and a forked muzzle (light / standard / ER by size)

ac / uac / lbx.what: receiver box, side ammo feed, barrel with a muzzle brake; Ultra AC twin barrels; LB-X a thicker barrel with an underside rail; AC/2 to AC/20 by size

gauss.what: triangular tube with three coil rings

mg / flamer / rotary.what: machine gun: small housing, twin barrels, ammo box; flamer: tank and nozzle; rotary: a drum and three barrels

missile_rack.what: chamfered frame, lid line, tube mouths as dark recesses with a colored rim, stripe on top and side; size from the tube count

_corrections: 2026-11-03: the chart cell first read as LINESMAN is the MAULER (90 t); Daniel supplied a Mauler model. There is no Linesman in these notes any more.

hard_sf_pass._about: Three critique passes (2026-11-03) from the point of view of a hard-SF military-hardware fan; what each fixed. Built items are in the generator or the viewer.

paint_schemes.what: steel, desert, olive, urban, arctic, navy; auto picks one per unit from its name; weathering darkens toward the feet and undersides

gunmetal_weapons.what: barrels, housings and receivers are gunmetal (class gm); the weapon class color is only a marking: laser lens ring, PPC coil rings, AC band, Gauss rings, flamer tank

waist_joint.what: a dark inner ring between pelvis and torso on flat torsos (not on dome / canopy bodies)

radiator_panel.what: a finned heat-rejection panel on the back of the torso, more fins from 60 t and 85 t

hydraulics.what: a piston and sleeve across the knee of humanoid legs; a long hip-to-hock hydraulic on chicken legs

arm_girth_and_hands.what: arm width and hands grow with tonnage (x0.92 to x1.42), so heavy 'Mechs do not have noodle arms

foot_size.what: feet grow with tonnage (x0.92 to x1.47): ground pressure reads right

plate_seams.what: two seams across the chest, no wider than the torso at that height

still_open: sensor clusters and a visible actuator at every joint
legs and arms are still smooth slabs without plating breakup

hard_sf_pass_2._about: Second round of hard-SF review (Daniel, 2026-11-03: 'knees are cubes with corners cut off', 'missile boxes stuck on the chest', 'every back plate is the same striped board', 'Banshee legs are stacked blocks'). Audit list and what was done.
audit: knees, elbows and every joint were chamfered cubes (the mesh cap for limbs)
legs were tubes with cube ends; the slab legs were literal stacked boxes
missile boxes were free cubes bolted to the chest, shoulders and forearms
the back plate was one identical striped board on every torso, ignoring torso shape and heat sinks
torsos were bare cuboids with sharp edges and flat fronts
arms were slabs with cube elbows

oriented_blocks.what: B3.obox: an oriented tapered armor block between two points; legs and arms are made of these, not tubes and cubes

cylinder_joints.what: hips, knees, ankles, hocks and elbows are short cylinders across the figure; the mesh builder makes every limb segment a faceted cylinder along its own axis (8 sides, 12 for joints and weapons) and a point a low-poly ball

armored_legs.what: thigh with a front plate, pointed kneecap guard, shin with a calf bulge and front plate, overlapping lapped shin plates on slab legs, hydraulic piston and sleeve

flush_launchers.what: missile racks on the chest are recessed behind a bezel (only the cover and tube mouths show); arm racks lie along the forearm instead of hanging under it

back_modules.what: five rear modules by name hash or the back tag (fins, hump reactor housing, twin exhaust stacks, engine cowl, framed vent), sized by the unit's heat sinks and fitted to the torso's rear face, taper and plan

chest_plates.what: a raised shield plate over the chest and a plate on each side torso; torso sections have cut side edges

still_open: torso silhouettes are still box-like; real hulls need compound curves and layered armor
arms are still blocks with cube-like hands
head and cockpit: no canopy frame, hatch or sensor cluster
no decals, markings or stencil text
no cabling, no visible actuators at the shoulder
the viewer lighting is flat; no ambient occlusion

design_principles._about: Daniel, 2026-11-03. How a 'Mech is built in this setting; the generator should follow it.
design_principles.skeleton_muscle_shell: A unit is a SKELETON driven by MYOMER muscle; weapons and armor go on top. Armor is a SHELL built around the skeleton, with some sections expanded for equipment or thicker armor. So 'blocky' is not the setting's prominent look. An arm can be an elephant's trunk: pure muscle in an exoskeleton shell (built: `arm_style: trunk`, the Mad Cat). The torsos and limbs are NOT yet built as shells over a skeleton; they are still boxes and tapered blocks.
design_principles.fusion_power: Fusion powered: no exhaust stacks unless chosen (the `stacks` back module is tag-only now).
design_principles.myomer_not_hydraulics: Myomer powered: muscle bundles (three thin parallel cables and a clamp) cross the knees and the hock; `pistons: true` draws pistons and sleeves for units where people would expect them (Daniel dislikes them: they imply hydraulics).
design_principles.weapon_bulk_follows_mass: A weapon's drawn bulk follows its mass (cube root, 0.55-1.9 around 3 t); weapon masses are Claude's recall of the construction rules (not in the indexed Core), art only.
design_principles.weapon_slots: Arm hardpoints are slots: the heaviest group in the centre slot, the next below, the third above; leave slots empty. Hand arms carry the weapon on the outside of the forearm; weapon arms get a housing sized by the gun.
design_principles.colors: Cockpit glass is blue (class ck); missiles are violet (class wm); energy red, ballistic amber.
design_principles.scaling_law: Equal mass, equal volume (Daniel, 2026-11-03). After a model is built, INTEGRATION__token_mesh.calibrate measures its real body volume (the union of the convex solids on a grid, weapons excluded) and scales width and depth so volume = DENSITY (0.0037 levels^3 per ton) x tons. Height is the rules curve (2 x (t/100)^(1/3) levels, 3 x (t/200)^(1/3) superheavy). All 47 chart units land within 3.47 to 4.01 e-3 per ton (2.3 percent spread); tests/test_token_volume.py guards it. The `girth`, `bodyd`, `bodyh` tags change SHAPE only now: calibration removes any volume they add.
design_principles.real_scale: 1 level = 6 m (the Atlas is 12 m tall = 2 levels), so 10 px of the drawing = 1 m. Missile tubes are sized from meters: LRM mouth 0.18 m (at most 0.2: a 25/3 kg missile), SRM 0.23 m (at most 0.25), MRM 0.143 m (an MRM missile is half an LRM's mass, so its diameter is 0.794 of an LRM's). Every missile tube in the generator (standalone racks, the Archer's and Mauler's launcher boxes, the Mad Cat's wing bays, centre-torso racks) uses `tube_px` / `rack_cells`; boxes are sized to hold the real tubes, not tubes to fill the box.
design_principles.bulk_by_structure: Daniel, 2026-11-04: each location's bulk, before its weapons and equipment, follows its internal structure points, the head's counted 1.5 times (data/token_densities.json bulk_rule; INTEGRATION__shell_items.budgets). The whole 'Mech's base volume is unchanged, only shared out differently.

shell_mapping._about: Skeleton-and-shell builder (INTEGRATION__shell.py, 2026-11-04, phase 1). Every reference-tag term and what it does to the new builder's parameters. Daniel's rule: a term the system cannot express is flagged here and kept in data/token_reference_tags.json; it is never dropped silently. Status: expressed / approximated / FLAGGED.

archetype.humanoid: expressed: leg 0.46 and torso 0.32 of the height, knee forward (ARCH)
archetype.bird: expressed: digitigrade chain (hip, knee forward, hock back, ankle), leg 0.50, torso 0.29 and 0.035 forward
archetype.martian: approximated: the humanoid chain with leg 0.54 and torso 0.28 (the hash can pick it; a reverse-knee skeleton is phase 3)
archetype.dog / lizard / quad / tripod: FLAGGED for Daniel: the shell builder (phase 1) cannot express it yet; the tag is kept and ignored, not dropped (phase 3; such units still use the old block builder)

torso.ovoid: expressed: plan bulge +0.2, depth 0.95 of width
torso.slab: expressed: width x0.9, height x1.1, depth 0.78
torso.dome: approximated: bulge +0.22, top narrowed to 0.82, height x1.05 (no separate dome solid yet)
torso.canopy: approximated: ovoid body with bulge +0.24; the wing bays of the old builder are NOT drawn (missiles mount on the torso rails) - FLAGGED

profile.upright / sloped / lean / wedge_up / bel: expressed: the side polygon of every torso section (T.PROFILES)
profile.tall_slab: expressed: the upright polygon, width x0.88, height x1.12
profile.hunch / stepped: FLAGGED: drawn as upright; the hump / second step solid of the old builder is not built yet

head_mount.top: expressed (drop 0.05 of the head's height into the torso)
head_mount.notch: approximated: forward on the chest, drop 0.45; no notch is cut into the torso

head_shape.box / dome / wedge / visor / skull: expressed: the head's side polygon (HEAD_PROF); skull adds a jaw plate

shoulders.boom: expressed: the shoulder dome is 22 percent bigger

shell_mapping.panels / surface / back / vents / stacks: FLAGGED: panel lines, the rear module and stacks of the old builder are not drawn; heat-sink items draw louvred vent panels on the torso rear or sides instead

legs.slab: expressed: wide plates, leg width / depth 1.6

shell_mapping.hips: FLAGGED: the flared hip of the old builder; the pelvis block and skirt plates replace it

arm_style.long_barrel: approximated: thicker, longer forearm with no hand; the guns come from the unit file
arm_style.trunk: expressed: six overlapping collars curving forward, no hand
arm_style.a_frame: approximated: elbows and wrists splayed outward

kit.tall_launchers / launchers: FLAGGED: launchers are the unit's own missile items on the torso rails; the tall standing boxes of the old builder are not drawn
kit.corner_pods / spar / fins / ears / tail_: FLAGGED for Daniel: the shell builder (phase 1) cannot express it yet; the tag is kept and ignored, not dropped

shell_mapping.hands: approximated: a fist for any hand; pincer / ball variants FLAGGED (ball via arm_style only)
shell_mapping.antennas / antenna: expressed: thin rods on the head
shell_mapping.girth / bodyd / bodyh / legscale / armsc: expressed: width, depth, torso height, legs, arms scale; volume still comes from the budgets, so a larger value changes SHAPE only where it can
shell_mapping.asym: approximated: the side torsos and arms differ because their budgets (their items) differ; the tag itself is FLAGGED (no extra bigger arm)
shell_mapping.crouch: expressed: legs 0.93 of the height, knees forward x2.2
shell_mapping.feet: FLAGGED: thrusters; every foot is a plain heel-to-toe block with a top plate
shell_mapping.physical: FLAGGED: hand weapons (hatchet, sword) are not drawn by the shell builder yet

facet_blocks._about: Faceted look (INTEGRATION__shell_facet.py, 2026-11-04): the humanoid's block library. A tag picks a block where it says something (TAG_PICKS); otherwise a byte of the name hash per slot picks, so untagged units still get a stable combination. The choice is in model['blocks'] and the viewer's info panel.
facet_blocks.leg: prism (eight-sided) / slab (six-sided, wide and shallow) / pillar (twelve-sided, even) / greave (flared armoured shin). Tags: legs slab -> slab, pillar -> pillar, heavy -> greave; kit round_blocks -> pillar.
facet_blocks.knee: drum / cap (a small plate over the knee front) / guard (a tall plate, the Atlas kit's knee). Tag: legs slab -> guard.
facet_blocks.foot: heel_toe (heel block and two toes) / wedge (one block, low at the toe) / three_toe. Tags: feet thrusters or legs pillar -> wedge.
facet_blocks.pauldron: box / slant (a pad sloping outward and down) / drum (across the joint) / collar (no pauldron). Tags: kit pauldrons -> box, kit round_blocks -> drum, shoulders flush -> collar.
facet_blocks.forearm: octagon / square / round (the forearm's section). Tag: kit round_blocks -> round.
facet_blocks.torso, head, launchers, hump, gun pods: not slot blocks yet: chosen by profile, head_mount / head_shape, kit tall_launchers / launchers, profile hunch / stepped, and arms without hand actuators (body_humanoid).
facet_blocks.pose: stride (left leg forward, right back, knees bent, 7 degree lean) / ready (knees bent, 4 degrees) / crouch (deep bend, 10 degrees). Tag: crouch -> crouch. The bird body uses stride / ready (staggered or level legs) under its own pitch.
facet_blocks.torso: v_chest / box / slab / wedge / round, each built as THREE parts that fit together (Daniel, 2026-11-04): a centre torso a little forward and two side torsos a little set back, each its own block with cut edges (a seam where they meet), each as wide as its own budget needs at 0.36 of the height deep (TORSO_PARTS, torso_pieces). The round block (a faceted ovoid, the old blocks' UrbanMech body) is one solid cut into its three parts. The centre torso is at most 1.25 times the side torsos' depth (no cross from above). Tags as before.
facet_blocks.housing: none / housing: a raised housing on the side torso with the heaviest gun, sized by that gun (1.9 x its width and height, 0.85 x its length), its front face carrying the gun. A standard block (Daniel, 2026-11-04: no one-off hump). Tag: profile hunch / stepped -> housing; by name hash only when that gun is 6 t or more.
facet_blocks.missiles: face (racks flush in the side torso's front) / bay (racks in the side torso's upper front, aimed forward and about 20 degrees up for the ballistic arc, each behind a door hinged at the top of its opening and swung up: the Archer's tall 'boxes' are these doors, per Daniel) / post (the bird body: one launcher on a post). Tags: kit tall_launchers / launchers -> bay.
facet_blocks.arm: for arms without a hand actuator: pod (upper arm down, the forearm a gun pod aimed forward) / straight (the gun lines up with the upper arm straight out of the shoulder: the JagerMech, per Daniel). Tag: arm_style long_barrel -> straight. Arms with hands are always bent with a fist.
facet_blocks.hips_and_waist: Not a slot: every faceted 'Mech has a pelvis block between the hips (two halves, by the hip actuators), a hip joint drum at each side, and a vertical waist drum (the torso-twist actuator) that the torso stands on.
facet_blocks.shoulder_rule: Not a slot: shoulder joints at least 1.22 times the hips' outer edge from the centre line (tiny arms excepted); a side torso widens to reach that and gets shallower to keep its volume.
facet_blocks.weapon_clearance: Not a slot: the space ahead of every muzzle (1.2 m) must be clear of the body; a blocked weapon slides forward, then moves to another rail of its location.
